items.item_text: Base Certification requirement (option A or B) A) CRCST from Healthcare Sterile Processing Association (HSPA) B) CSPDT from The Certification Board of Sterile Processing and Distribution (CBSPD)
CSIS from The Certification Board of Sterile Processing and Distribution (CBSPD)
Certification in Endoscope Reprocessing (CER) from Healthcare Sterile Processing Association (HSPA)
Certified Endoscope Reprocessor (CFER) from The Certification Board of Sterile Processing and Distribution (CBSPD)
Bachelor’s degree in a healthcare ﬁeld preferred.
Five (5) years of recent demonstrated experience working as a Sterile Technician in a Sterile Processing Department.
Minimum (1) year experience as a Trainer/Educator, including experience developing and implementing educational and training plans for various roles in the department.
Demonstrated experience practicing and implementing operational practices according to AAMI Standards and Guidelines.
Experience with disinfection, sterilization, packaging, and infection control practices and principles.
Experience developing and implementing educational and training plans for various roles in the department.
Experience planning, coordinating, and conducting in-services for staff to ensure safe, current and appropriate industry practices.
Experience and a knowledge base of a surgical atmosphere.
Demonstrated experience developing and updating competencies that reﬂect the skills required to perform various work.

The Sterile Processing Educator will develop and provide orientation, continuing education, competency and training, and staff development for the Sterile Processing Unit. This positions’ primary responsibility is for developing, implementing, tracking and managing all departmental educational activities that include training programs /curriculum and instruction for both newly hired and current staff members. This position will be responsible for writing, reviewing, and updating unit competencies and assisting management in updating and or developing department policy and procedures. Provides support to all staff to maintain Continuing Education Unit (CEU) opportunities offered to employees as well as assistance in certiﬁcation / re-certiﬁcation.
60% - Education and Training
Incumbent must be able to organize departmental in services and coordinate vendor in-services for continuous training.
20% - Administrative Coordination
10% - Professional Development
Able to use a computer to communicate with email, retrieve data and create/edit competencies, power point presentations, and policy & procedures.
CIS from HSPA from Healthcare Sterile Processing Association (HSPA)
Able to work well under deadlines in a fast-paced changing environment and perform multiple tasks effectively and concurrently.
Able to apply/enforce policy and procedure when making decisions.

With minimal supervision and with signiﬁcant autonomy, able to identify problems and initiates appropriate actions. Demonstrates good judgment and independent decision-making in handling situations not covered by written or verbal instructions. Maintain conﬁdentiality.
Extensive knowledge of AAMI (American Association of Medical Instrumentation) recommended practices and regulatory agency guidelines as it pertains to sterile processing.
Ability to maintain current knowledge on industry practices and guidelines to ensure compliance with regulatory agencies and inspections.
Working knowledge on training and development, performance management and workplace learning. Ability to apply knowledge to achieve successful organizational outcomes.
Effective verbal and written communication skills to interact and present to the target and diverse audience.
Ability to set work priorities and establish/complete deadlines.
Ability to establish effective interpersonal & working relationships with all staff.

Must possess effective presentation skills, utilize principles of adult learning theory, and model professional behavior. Detailed oriented, with strong organizational and project management skills, and the ability to work collaboratively in teams.
Ability to make independent clinical decisions in patient care matters. Ability to work accurately and quickly under pressure. Maintain an awareness of changes in procedures and protocols.
Ability to maintain an awareness of changes in procedures and protocols.
Ability to assist in planning and organizing workﬂow well; meet established turn-around-times, and deadlines.
Ability to integrate the understanding of UCDHS’ goals and objectives, commitments and projections within a service-oriented healthcare environment.

Ability to organize and perform multiple tasks concurrently. Maintain a clean, organized work area. Ability to prioritize/reorganize work in response to STAT/Emergency requests. Ability to set priorities, organize work independently and for others.
